content: The physical examination for diabetic foot care, as recommended by the American Diabetes Association (ADA), involves the following steps: 1. Conduct a thorough inspection of the feet to evaluate the condition of the skin, checking for any signs of compromised skin integrity, the presence of lesions, or structural deformities. 2. Perform screening for peripheral arterial disease (PAD) by palpating the pedal pulses. If the ankle-brachial index (ABI) is found to be decreased, the patient should be referred for further vascular evaluation. 3. Assess sensory function and reflexes in the feet. This includes the use of a 10-gram monofilament to test for protective sensation and additional tests, such as temperature discrimination, to evaluate sensory deficits.
